title: Man. Post. Cap. II §XIX: Placeus — Paul’s sense; subordinate cause; mediate reatus
pass_a_gloss: PLAC. Did I take the word of imputing in that sense in which Paul took it, when he said foreskin is imputed for circumcision, or not? The Learned Man does not deny it. Therefore I did not play in that word, unless he wishes the Apostle likewise to have played in the same word. For I used it in that signification whose most weighty author I have, Paul himself. But here, he says, it is not about the imputation of any thing whatsoever, but about the imputation of another's sin. What then afterward? Is there something that prohibits that word, in which sense it is used of some other thing, from being used also of sin? But by the imputation of sin is not to be understood a comparison of diverse sins by diverse persons or a parity among diverse sins. What is this to me? Did I understand by the imputation of Adam's disobedience such a comparison, or parity? Certainly not. Diverse sins committed by diverse persons are both actual sins; the vice inhering in us from the origin is not an actual sin, but only habitual. Of those diverse sins one is not the cause of the other: whereas yet the actual disobedience was the cause of the habitual inhering in us. Therefore those diverse sins are compared as, so to speak, coordinated, but these disobediences as subordinated. Since therefore Adam's disobedience is the cause of the vice inhering in us, and this is the cause of our guilt, it is necessary that Adam's disobedience be the cause of our guilt, at least mediate. Therefore we are guilty on account of the vice inhering in us immediately, and by that mediating on account of that actual disobedience of Adam, of which that inhering vice is a certain habitual consent and approval and communion: so that for that cause it can more properly be said to be imputed to us unto sin than foreskin unto circumcision, on account of the kept δικαιώματα of the Law.
pass_b_english: Placeus: Did I take 'impute' as Paul took it when he said foreskin is imputed for circumcision (Romans 2:26)—yes or no? The learned man will not deny it. Then I was not gaming the word, unless he wants Paul gaming it too. I used Paul's sense; he is my heaviest warrant. But here, says he, we speak not of imputing just any thing, but of imputing another's sin. So what? May a word used of some other matter not also be used, in that same sense, of sin? He adds that imputing sin must not mean lining up different sins by different persons, or a parity of sins for punishment or guilt. How does that touch me? Did I mean by Adam's-disobedience imputation such a lineup or parity? No. Different persons' different sins are both actual; the vice born into us is not actual but only habitual. Neither of those different sins causes the other—yet Adam's actual disobedience caused the habitual vice in us. So those sins sit side by side (coordinated, if I may say so); these disobediences sit under one another. Adam's disobedience causes our inhering vice; that vice causes our guilt; therefore Adam's disobedience causes our guilt—at least as a mediate cause. We are guilty at once for the vice in us, and through that medium for Adam's actual disobedience—of which the inhering vice is a kind of habitual consent, approval, and share. That is why it may more properly be said imputed to us unto sin than foreskin unto circumcision for the Law's kept δικαιώματα.
source_text: PLAC. Sumpfine verbum imputandi eo sensu quo illud Paulus sumpsit, cum dixit praeputium imputari in circuncisionem, nec-ne? Non negat Vir doctus. Ergo in eo verbo non lusi, nisi velit in eodem verbo similiter lusisse Apostolum. In ea enim significatione illud usurpavi, cujus gravissimum habeo autorem, ipsum Paulum. At hic, inquit, non de imputatione cujusvis rei agitur, sed de imputatione peccati alieni. Quid tum postea? Est-ne aliquid quod prohibeat illud verbum, quo sensu de alia aliqua re usurpatur, eodem etiam usurpari de peccato? At per imputationem peccati non est intelligenda collatio diversorum peccatorum a diversis personis patratorum vel paritas inter diversa peccata. Quid hoc ad me? An per imputationem inobedientiae Adami talem intellexi vel collationem, vel paritatem? Non certe. Diversa peccata a diversis personis patrata sunt ambo peccata actualia; vitium nobis ab origine inhaerens non est peccatum actuale, sed habituale tantum. Illorum peccatorum diversorum unum non est causa alterius: cum tamen inobedientia actualis nobis inhaerentis habitualis causa fuerit. Itaque conferuntur illa diversa peccata, tanquam ut, ita loquar, coordinata, hae vero inobedientiae tanquam subordinatae. Cum ergo inobedientia Adami sit causa vitii nobis inhaerentis, & hoc sit causa reatus nostri, necesse est inobedientiam Adami causam esse nostri reatus, saltem mediatam. Itaque nos esse reos ob vitium nobis inhaerens immediate, eoque mediante ob inobedientiam illam actualem Adami, cujus vitium illud inhaerens habitualis quaedam est consensus & approbatio, & communio: ut ob eam causam magis proprie nobis in peccatum dici possit imputari, quam praeputium in circuncisionem, ob servata Legis δικαιώματα.
